verdicts.note: Attacked toward +1 as a continuation of an expiring levy for an existing contracted service (S1, S12). A plain renewal at the same level would be +1. This one raises the ceiling from $0.15 to $0.28 per $1,000, an 87% increase, and more than doubles the 2025 rate of about $0.12 (S1, S6), for six years. That is a substantial levy increase, which taxes pole_b covers, so +2 holds. S1 and S6 exist in the dossier frontmatter and support the figures. spending and local-control are rightly unmapped, as the dossier's lean notes explain.

what_it_does matches the dossier: who votes (S8-S10), six years from 2027, the Lewiston contract, replacing the levy that expires at the end of 2026 (S1), the 118-146 August failure (S3), and the simple-majority threshold for a later levy (S5). cost_line matches S1 and S6: $0.28 up from $0.15, a 2025 rate of about $0.12, and $28 per $100,000. con_summary is accurate: no statement or campaign against (S1, S2, S14), nearly doubles the maximum (15 to 28 cents), and 146/264 = 55% no (S3). pro_summary overreaches in one phrase. The dossier attributes to the supporters only that the levy 'cannot be used for other county expenses' and that EMS stops without it (S12). It does not say the levy is the 'only dedicated funding' for ALS ambulance service. Suggest: 'A group of rural residents says the levy pays for the advanced life support ambulance contract, cannot be used for other county expenses, and that without it EMS would stop when the Lewiston contract runs out.' The Life Flight point (S11, S12) and the commissioners' informational outreach (S8) are accurate.
